findings.issue_text: postMessage origin check in embed.js uses substring containment (indexOf === -1) instead of exact equality, allowing an attacker origin that is a prefix/substring of discourseUrl to spoof discourse-resize messages and control iframe height

TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read via open-uri with no scheme validation (unlike TopicEmbed.import which enforces ^https?://), risking SSRF or pipe-to-shell if called with unvalidated input such as from disqus.thor

PollFeed job calls CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) which raises NoMethodError when a feed item lacks a content element, and since sidekiq retry is disabled, this aborts the entire hourly run for that batch

TopicEmbed.import performs a check-then-create on embed_url without locking, allowing concurrent imports of the same URL to race on the unique index and raise an unhandled RecordNotUnique after the post has already been created

embed_controller.rb applies discourse_expires_in 1.minute unconditionally to both the loading placeholder and real content responses, causing a cached loading page to be served for up to a minute after real content is available
The -c/--category option in lib/tasks/disqus.thor was removed outright instead of deprecated, silently breaking existing script invocations that pass --category
embed.js concatenates discourseUrl + "embed/best?..." assuming a trailing slash, producing a malformed URL if discourseUrl lacks one
No test coverage exists for TopicEmbed.import_remote, leaving the Readability-based remote-fetch/parsing logic untested

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read via open-uri with no scheme validation (unlike TopicEmbed.import which enforces ^https?://), risking SSRF or pipe-to-shell if called with unvalidated input such as from disqus.thor

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (open-uri) without validating that `url` is an `http`/`https` URL. This contrasts with `TopicEmbed.import`, which explicitly rejects non-`^https?://` URLs. `import_remote` is invoked from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`) where `t[:link]` comes from parsed import data and is not validated in this code path, so non-HTTP schemes (or other open-uri-supported targets) could be fetched. That is a real, verifiable security risk (SSRF / unintended local/other-scheme reads) introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import performs a check-then-create on embed_url without locking, allowing concurrent imports of the same URL to race on the unique index and raise an unhandled RecordNotUnique after the post has already been created

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, it first does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, proceeds to create a post and then `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. Because there is a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`), two concurrent callers can both observe `embed.blank?` and both attempt `create!`, causing the loser to raise an `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`/uniqueness violation. There is no rescue/handling for that exception in the method, so it can bubble up and fail the job/request. (The transaction likely rolls back the post insert, but the unhandled exception/race still exists.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb applies discourse_expires_in 1.minute unconditionally to both the loading placeholder and real content responses, causing a cached loading page to be served for up to a minute after real content is available

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is called at the end of the action regardless of whether the response is the real embed content (`best.html.erb`) or the placeholder (`render 'loading'`). That means the loading page can be returned with cache headers allowing it to be cached for up to 60 seconds. If a `TopicEmbed` becomes available shortly after the first request, a subsequent reload (including the JS `document.location.reload()` in `loading.html.erb`) may still be satisfied from cache during that TTL, delaying display of real content. The finding is directly grounded in the unconditional `discourse_expires_in` placement in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The -c/--category option in lib/tasks/disqus.thor was removed outright instead of deprecated, silently breaking existing script invocations that pass --category

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the line defining `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` was removed, along with the logic that read `options[:category]` and set `category_id` for `PostCreator`. With this diff, any existing invocations of the Thor task that pass `-c/--category` will now fail due to an unrecognized option and the task no longer supports selecting a category via CLI. The finding’s core point (breaking existing invocations) is directly verifiable from the diff, though it likely won’t be “silent” (Thor typically errors on unknown options).

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js concatenates discourseUrl + "embed/best?..." assuming a trailing slash, producing a malformed URL if discourseUrl lacks one

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the iframe URL is built via simple concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + ...`. There is no insertion/normalization of a `/` between `discourseUrl` and `embed/best`, so if `discourseUrl` is provided without a trailing slash (e.g., `https://forum.example.com`), the resulting URL becomes `https://forum.example.comembed/best?...`, which is malformed and will break embedding. The diff does not show any guarantee that `discourseUrl` always ends with `/`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage exists for TopicEmbed.import_remote, leaving the Readability-based remote-fetch/parsing logic untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (uses `ruby-readability` and `open(url).read` parsing) in `app/models/topic_embed.rb`, but the added specs (`spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`, `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb`, etc.) only exercise `TopicEmbed.import` and mock/stub around retrieval; none call `TopicEmbed.import_remote` or validate its Readability/open-uri behavior. So the remote fetch/parsing path is untested in this diff.
